method: Independent readonly diff and test-boundary review; no repeated tests or native Windows execution
checks: New-document readiness checks renderer initialization independently from initial menu entry, permitting direct query navigation into an actually rendered race.

Native epoch must exactly match immutable DOM epoch, advance monotonically, and carry a newer finite timestamp. New document requires ready, allowed renderer and matching WebGL major, finite frames>1, integer poll>1, known consistent stage/paused state, dictionary gameplay and no reported errors.

Same-document reads retain actual poll-growth requirements and reject game/controller null safely. Old-host fallback applies only when both snapshots omit epoch; partial identity does not become legacy compatibility.
Freshness does not change any original plan expectation. Warmup and countdown may be fresh but still fail the running expectation; only actual running satisfies both.
Tests cover wrong renderer/version, missing frames/polls, runtime error, stale timestamp, old DOM identity and null snapshots. Original attempt1 and attempt2 initial source/results remain retained.
limitations: The exact native document/bootstrap/SDK sequence remains subject to the next frozen-source Windows run.
